candidates.evidence: धूमः (smoke) / रात्रिः (night) / कृष्णः (the dark fortnight) / दक्षिणायनम् (the southern course)

angle_en: Some routes only delay return; they do not end the cycle.

en.intro: Krishna now names the opposite path, the one that leads back to birth. Listen to the sequence of images that mark it.
en.notice: The verse lists four images: smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the southern half-year. The yogi who departs there reaches lunar light and returns.
en.next: The next verse states that these two paths are the eternal ways of the world, one leading to no-return, the other to return.
en.meaning: In the path ruled by smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the six months of the southern course, the yogi who departs there returns after reaching the moon's light.

hi.intro: कृष्ण अब उस विपरीत मार्ग का वर्णन करते हैं, जो जन्म की ओर वापस ले जाता है। सुनिए उन छवियों को जो इसे दर्शाती हैं।
hi.meaning: जिस मार्गमें धूमका अधिपति देवता, रात्रिका अधिपति देवता, कृष्णपक्षका अधिपति देवता और छह महीनोंवाले दक्षिणायनका अधिपति देवता है, शरीर छोड़कर उस मार्गसे गया हुआ योगी चन्द्रमाकी ज्योतिको प्राप्त होकर लौट आता है
hi.notice: यह श्लोक चार छवियों की एक सूची प्रस्तुत करता है: धुआँ, रात, कृष्ण पक्ष और दक्षिणायन। यहाँ योगी चन्द्रमा की ज्योति तक पहुँचकर वापस लौटता है।
hi.next: संसार में दो सनातन पथ हैं, एक जो मोक्ष की ओर ले जाता है और दूसरा जो पुनर्जन्म की ओर ले जाता है।

issues: borrowed: "The verse is built from a list of four images: smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the southern half-year. Each one is a sign of fading light, and together they point to a path that ends in return rather than release." (The 'fading light' interpretation is not in the source verse (which simply lists the elements) or the known Mahabharata story; it is a subjective inference. More importantly, the notice presents the 'return' conclusion as if it were contained within the verse itself, rather than being the overall teaching of the chapter. However, looking strictly at the provided text, the 'fading light' and 'return' are interpretive. The actual borrowed content is in the next field: 'The next verse confirms these two paths as the eternal ways of the world, one leading to no-return, the other to return.' This is a direct paraphrase of the NEXT verse (8.26), presented as a property of the current verse's notice.)

borrowed: "अगला श्लोक इन दोनों मार्गों को संसार के दो सनातन पथों के रूप में पुष्टि करता है, एक मोक्ष की ओर और दूसरा पुनर्जन्म की ओर।" (This sentence is the Hindi version of the NEXT verse (8.26). It is presented as the 'next' field of the current verse, but it is actually the content of the subsequent verse, not a description of what the current verse says.)

unsupported: "योगी सकाम मनुष्य चन्द्रमाकी ज्योतिको प्राप्त होकर" (The source does not state that the yogi who departs via this path is a 'sakama manushya' (a person with unfulfilled desires). This is an unsupported addition.)
